aileron.instructions: Choose the absolute aileron command using `flight.roll_deg` and `flight.p_rad_s` FIRST. Positive roll_deg means RIGHT bank; negative means LEFT bank. Positive p_rad_s means rolling RIGHT. Arrest a bank of 3 degrees or more BEFORE chasing runway alignment or sideways velocity; do not increase excessive bank. Only with bank below 3 degrees, first BRAKE sideways motion using motion.cross_track_rate_mps: above +0.5 m/s needs LEFT bank; below -0.5 m/s needs RIGHT bank, even if still on the opposite side of centerline. Wings level alone does NOT stop sideways drift. Only when sideways speed is below 0.5 m/s, use position to intercept: offset above +2m needs LEFT bank, below -2m needs RIGHT bank. Keep corrective bank small, about 2 degrees. Positive runway.centerline_offset_m means POSITION right of runway; positive runway.heading_error_deg means nose POINTING right, NOT position. Absolute trim aileron is -0.15; more positive rolls right, more negative rolls left. Use current `flight` and `runway` state to choose one matching physical correction; do not select trim when the aircraft is diverging.

criteria.0: Strong LEFT roll correction: roll_deg above +8 (large RIGHT bank), especially p_rad_s positive. Recovery outranks runway offset.
criteria.1: Moderate LEFT roll correction: roll_deg +3 to +8 degrees (RIGHT bank); reduce bank before it grows.
criteria.2: Only with bank between -3 and +3 degrees: gentle LEFT roll, moving RIGHT faster than +0.5 m/s and roll>-2; OR nearly stationary sideways, position offset>+2m and roll>-2; OR centered with small RIGHT bank. NOT when moving LEFT faster than -0.5 m/s.
criteria.3: Only with bank between -3 and +3 degrees: maintain current small bank: already banking LEFT about -2 degrees to brake RIGHT motion, or RIGHT about +2 degrees to brake LEFT motion; OR centered with sideways speed below 0.5 m/s and wings level.
criteria.4: Only with bank between -3 and +3 degrees: gentle RIGHT roll, moving LEFT faster than -0.5 m/s and roll<+2; OR nearly stationary sideways, position offset<-2m and roll<+2; OR centered with small LEFT bank. NOT when moving RIGHT faster than +0.5 m/s.
criteria.5: Moderate RIGHT roll correction: roll_deg -3 to -8 degrees (LEFT bank); reduce bank before it grows.
criteria.6: Strong RIGHT roll correction: roll_deg below -8 (large LEFT bank), especially p_rad_s negative. Recovery outranks runway offset.

elevator.instructions: Choose ABSOLUTE elevator during APPROACH. Positive commands pitch nose DOWN, negative nose UP. Follow the3-degree glidepath before threshold; normal sink1.5-3m/s is not an emergency. Modest nose-negative pitch can be normal while descending. Do not flare early. Use the matching approach criterion, considering vertical_speed_mps, pitch_deg and q_rad_s. Above glidepath and shallow descent needs more nose-down; arrest an actual worsening dive. Use current `flight` and `runway` state to choose one matching physical correction; do not select trim when the aircraft is diverging.

criteria.0: Emergency nose-UP: severe dive sinking faster than8m/s, or pitch below -15 degrees and falling.
criteria.1: Strong nose-UP: deep dive sinking6-8m/s, with pitch below -10 degrees.
criteria.2: Firm nose-UP: dive sinking5-6m/s, with pitch below -7 degrees.
criteria.3: Nose-UP recovery: sinking4.5-5m/s with nose below -5 and still falling.
criteria.4: Nose-UP support: sinking4-4.5m/s with negative pitch.
criteria.5: Moderate nose-UP support: sinking3.5-4m/s with negative pitch.
criteria.6: Mild nose-UP support: below glidepath and descending, or sink3-3.5m/s worsening with nose low.
criteria.7: Normal approach command: descent1-3m/s and modest pitch. Maintain normal descent; do not arrest it.
criteria.8: Moderate nose-DOWN: before threshold, above glidepath by more than0.5 degrees and sink shallower than2m/s; OR climbing/pitch rising excessively.
criteria.9: Strong nose-DOWN: steep climb faster than3m/s with pitch above10 degrees.

rudder.instructions: Select ABSOLUTE rudder command for C172 approach. Trim +0.09 counters propeller torque. Increasing yaw command turns nose LEFT; decreasing turns nose RIGHT. Positive heading error is pointing right of runway: increase rudder gently; negative heading error decrease. Damp yaw rate and beta sideslip. Near alignment use trim. Use current `flight` and `runway` state to choose one matching physical correction; do not select trim when the aircraft is diverging.

criteria.0: Strong yaw RIGHT: nose points far LEFT of runway heading.
criteria.1: Moderate yaw RIGHT: nose points LEFT of runway heading.
criteria.2: Gentle yaw RIGHT: nose points slightly LEFT of runway heading.
criteria.3: Trim yaw: nose aligned with runway and low yaw rate.
criteria.4: Gentle yaw LEFT: nose points slightly RIGHT of runway heading.
criteria.5: Moderate yaw LEFT: nose points RIGHT of runway heading.
criteria.6: Strong yaw LEFT: nose points far RIGHT of runway heading.

throttle.instructions: Select ABSOLUTE throttle for C172 approach. Aim approach airspeed 30 m/s; use about 0.5 at 30 m/s, add power if slow, reduce if fast. During FLARE reduce throttle to 0.25 or less during flare. Do not cut early while still high. Touchdown ideal airspeed 28m/s. Use current `flight` and `runway` state to choose one matching physical correction; do not select trim when the aircraft is diverging.

criteria.0: Idle for ground rollout or final flare with excessive airspeed.
criteria.2: Slightly reduced approach power for airspeed faster than 36 m/s; never when below glidepath.
criteria.3: Normal approach power at airspeed 29 to 36 m/s, phase APPROACH; maintain while not safely in flare.
criteria.4: Increased approach power for airspeed about 27 m/s.
criteria.5: High approach power for airspeed about 24 m/s.
criteria.6: Full power for dangerously low airspeed below 22 m/s.
